setlist_extra.title: Stuck Inside of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stella Blue** (3 reviews): The listener liked the Eyes of the World and Stella Blue pairing; The build-up to a beautiful Stella Blue left the reviewer and a friend speechless [9][12][13]
- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Peggy-O was a particularly good version; Jerry's tender, flowing notes throughout Peggy-O were exemplary [10][11]
- **To Lay Me Down** (2 reviews): To Lay Me Down was sweet, with Jerry's playing especially affecting; To Lay Me Down was a huge treat [10][13]
- **Space** (2 other sources): Phil plays a really nice bass solo at the start of Space [4][7]
- **Cold Rain & Snow** (1 review): The reviewer found the opening Cold Rain bland [11]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Minglewood mentions bayside girls, and Bobby nearly slipped on the Mountain View reference the second time through [11]
- **Spacey Tuning** (1 review): The spacey second-set opener led into a good Crazy Fingers [10]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Crazy Fingers was great [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Spacey Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Bass**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd88-10-02.sbd.sacks.7637.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 3/5 by 14 [1]
- **gd1988-10-02.169164.MountainView.CA.UltramatrixSBD.dolby.c.cm.marcus.miller.t-flac1648**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min [4]
- **gd1988-10-02.168661.superscopeEC7.ont.flac1644**: source not stated; 20 songs; 154 min [5]
- **gd1988-10-02.142490.s2.sbd.bm.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 12 songs; 106 min [7]

## Around the show

- Sunday crowds were often smaller than on Friday and Saturday, since many people partied hard earlier in the weekend [12]
- Brent played on fire all weekend, and the reviewer can hear themselves in the audience [19]
- In 1988 tapers were moved to Section 202, reserved seating directly behind the soundboard [5]
- The reviewer thought this was the musical high point of the Shoreline run [12]
- The taper's 1987 Shoreline tapes had more punch, helped by repeater towers on the lawn, which were absent in 1988 [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-10-02.sbd.sacks.7637.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Cass> DAT> CDR> EAC>SHN (seekable) [1]. Also: Soundboard to cassette to DAT to CDR to EAC to SHN, via Darrin Sacks to abgd and etree [1]
- **gd1988-10-02.169164.MountainView.CA.UltramatrixSBD.dolby.c.cm.marcus.miller.t-flac1648**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony WM-D6C/Maxell MA/Dolby C) [4]. Also: Ultramatrix soundboard with Dolby, converted from 24-bit/96k to 16-bit/44.1k FLAC [4]
- **gd1988-10-02.168661.superscopeEC7.ont.flac1644**: taped by OldNeumanntapr; transferred by OldNeumanntapr; source: OTS; SEC 202, Row E, Seat #20, Front Row Of Tapers Section; Superscope EC 7 Cardioid Condensers >Marantz PMD-430 [XLIIS] [5]. Also: Recorded by the taper on a Superscope EC7 as an audience tape [5]
- **gd1988-10-02.142490.s2.sbd.bm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Beta HiFi Master (Sony Betamax/TDK HS) [7]. Also: Healy mix soundboard with no ambient microphones; 16-bit, 44.1 kHz files; This source is missing the first set [7]
